# One Year After Pakistan Monsoon Floods 2022 (As of 31 August 2023)

## Attachments

- Download infographic (PDF | 8.59 MB) 

CONTEXT

One year after the disastrous floods that ravaged Pakistan in June 2022, submerging large parts of the country and impacting 33 million people. The government of Pakistan declared a national state of emergency. The catastrophe claimed the lives of more than 1,700 people and left over 12,000 injured. The United Nations and humanitarian organizations provided life-saving assistance to those affected. However, the recovery process is far from complete, and support will still be required.

SITUATION OVERVIEW

As of 31 August 2023, the Flood Response Plan 2022 (FRP) was US$563 million (69%) of the US$816 million requirement. In the last year, the Government and humanitarian organizations reached over 6.1 million people with life-saving assistance in 34 prioritized districts across Pakistan.

The humanitarian needs still remain high with more than 10.5 million people food insecure (IPC level-3 and Level-4); 4.5 million people without clean drinking water, 3.5 million children under five severely malnourished, and another 23 million children out of schools.

A pressing need for assistance persists in providing aid to both the susceptible communities that continue to reside in areas prone to flooding, as well as those who have yet to receive any support since the onset of the floods. These individuals are currently lacking essential services and the necessary assistance required to cope with their situation
